method: Structured JSON from the Gemini API, instructed by docs/PROJECT_VISION.md@main blob fe2f414774b7. Every cited URL was fetched; dead links and pages that never mention the character were removed, and feats, results, conditions and campaign tags that lost their source were moved to unknowns. All records provisional. Independent Claude review (2026-11-13): every record rebuilt from pages opened in review; Wikipedia citations replaced with fan-wiki pages where needed; records stay provisional.

characters.continuity: Rayman series (Ubisoft): Rayman (1995), Rayman 2: The Great Escape, Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc, Origins/Legends
characters.summary: Rayman is a limbless hero whose head, hands and feet float unattached to his torso. His signature attack is the telescopic fist, first granted by Betilla the fairy, which he hurls at enemies; he spins his hair like a helicopter rotor to glide, and temporary power-ups (the super helicopter) let him fly under control.

techniques: Telescopic fist (chargeable; gold and speed fist upgrades)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources beyond mobility (gliding away from hazards)

weaknesses: His powers can be taken from him: Mr Dark magically stole his telescopic fist power before their final battle, leaving him unable to punch until Electoons returned it
limitations: The normal helicopter ability is a glide, not sustained flight; controlled flight needs the temporary super helicopter power-up

sources.supports: Limbless body with head, hands and feet 'invisibly linked to his torso'; throwing his fists as projectiles; spinning his hair like a helicopter rotor to slow his descent; Rabbids taking his fists in the handheld Raving Rabbids.

Telescopic fist granted by Betilla in Rayman (1995); gold fists double its power, speed fists throw faster, charging increases power; grappling fist; replaced by energy-ball shooting in Rayman 2; returns in Rayman 3 and Origins/Legends.
Final battle of Rayman (1995): Mr Dark steals Rayman's fist power, Electoons return it, and Rayman defeats Mr Dark's three hybrid-monster forms, the last with a final punch to the head.

The super helicopter is a temporary power-up (Musician's flask in Rayman, Ly in Rayman 2) that 'allows you to fly while retaining control of your direction', as opposed to the normal helicopter glide.

feats.claim: Hurls his telescopic fist to defeat enemies at range; gold fists double its power and charging increases it.
Flew through lava corridors in Rayman 2 using the super helicopter power granted by Ly.

notableResults.note: Mr Dark first stole Rayman's fist power and attacked with walls of flame and fireballs; after Electoons returned the fist, Rayman beat his three hybrid-monster transformations, finishing him with a punch to the head of the third.

conditional.dependsOn: Temporary super helicopter power-up (Musician's flask, other potions, or Ly in Rayman 2)

campaignTags.claim: Spins his hair like a helicopter rotor to glide and slow his descent.

unknowns: Gemini's 'flight' tag was replaced by 'glide': the normal helicopter is a glide, and true flight needs a temporary power-up.
No documented height, durability feats, or results against Razorbeard, Andre or Reflux were verified in the opened sources.

characters.continuity: Overwatch / Overwatch 2 (Blizzard): game kit plus official story media
characters.summary: Reinhardt Wilhelm is a veteran German crusader clad in powered Crusader armor. He fights at close range with a rocket hammer, protects allies with a deployable energy Barrier Field, charges to pin enemies into walls, throws flaming Fire Strike projectiles, and knocks foes down with the Earthshatter shockwave.

mechanisms: Barrier Field energy shield (1500 health; regenerates after 2 seconds down)

weaknesses: Lost sight in his left eye at the Battle of Eichenwalde after an OR14 unit slashed him with a heat blade, so his left side is a blind side
mobility: Charge: rushes forward up to about 50 m
limitations: Cannot attack while holding Barrier Field, and it slows him by 30%
Barrier Field has finite health and breaks under sustained fire
Rocket Hammer reach is about 4 m

sources.supports: Ability kit (Rocket Hammer, Barrier Field 1500 health and 30% slow, Charge pin, Fire Strike flaming projectile, Earthshatter knockdown); described as 'Clad in powered armor' (Crusader armor, upgraded by Brigitte and Winston); lore: Eichenwalde eye wound, Asuncion hostage rescue, Romania Dragons, Paris Null Sector Titan.

feats.claim: Charges and pins the first enemy hit; a wall impact deals heavy damage.
Earthshatter knocks down enemies in a 50-degree cone in front of him for 3 seconds.
Charged into a hostage situation at the Palacio de Lopez in Asuncion against orders and saved 47 of 50 hostages.

notableResults.note: The Dragons beat Reinhardt badly at first.
He returned in new armor and drove them out of the area.
Team result: Reinhardt and Brigitte held it off until Tracer finished it.
He saved 47 hostages, but Hivemind escaped with the data.

campaignTags.claim: The Overwatch Wiki describes him as 'Clad in powered armor' (Crusader armor).
Powered Crusader armor and rocket hammer; under the owner ruling, powered armor earns tech.
Fire Strike launches a flaming projectile from his hammer.

unknowns: No documented height was verified, so giant-sized is not proposed.
Durability limits of the Crusader armor against high-end weaponry are not documented in the opened source.

characters.continuity: Street Fighter series (Capcom) main canon: Street Fighter through Street Fighter V
characters.summary: Ryu is a wandering Ansatsuken martial artist trained by Gouken. He fights with the Hadoken energy projectile, the rising Shoryuken and the spinning Tatsumaki Senpukyaku, plus super combos such as the Shinku Hadoken and Shin Shoryuken. He constantly struggles against the Satsui no Hado, the murderous dark side of his art.

mechanisms: The Shoryuken's start-up can evade projectiles

weaknesses: The Satsui no Hado inside him can be exploited: M. Bison used it to brainwash him by comparing it to his own Psycho Power (Alpha)
limitations: Refuses to use the Satsui no Hado, so he fights without its power unless it takes over

sources.supports: Ansatsuken style, Hadouken/Shoryuken/Tatsumaki, super combos (Shinkuu Hadouken, Shin Shoryuken, charged Denjin Hadouken), Shakunetsu Hadouken without setting himself on fire; results vs Sagat, Akuma, Ken, M. Bison (Alpha brainwashing), Oro, Alex, Hugo; Satsui no Hadou struggle.
Street Fighter V 'A Shadow Falls': Ryu controls the Satsui no Hado to deliver the final blow that reverts Necalli; Ken loses to Ryu at the end.

feats.claim: Has the most concentrated Hadouken of Gouken's students; only Akuma matches or surpasses it in some cases.
Can use the Shakunetsu Hadouken (a burning Hadoken) without setting himself on fire.

notableResults.note: Ryu nearly lost; later games show him giving in to the Satsui no Hado for the Metsu Shoryuken that scarred Sagat's chest.
Akuma beat him on Gokuentou but was only testing him.
Ken won and gave Ryu his red headband; Ryu won the rematch in Third Strike.
Rematch win.
Bison defeated and brainwashed him; Sagat's challenge broke it and Ryu, Ken and Sakura forced Bison to retreat.
Lost in the third World Warrior tournament.

notableResults.citation: Street Fighter V: A Shadow Falls
notableResults.note: Dhalsim intervened while the Hado took hold; Ryu then controlled the Satsui no Hado to land the final blow.

campaignTags.claim: Uses the Shakunetsu Hadouken, a burning fireball, without setting himself on fire.

unknowns: The Denjin Hadouken's electrical nature is not stated in the opened source, so no electric tag is proposed.
Results vs Seth and Gill were not verified.

characters.continuity: Street Fighter Alpha series and later appearances (Alpha 2, Capcom vs. SNK, Super Street Fighter IV Arcade Edition), plus Street Fighter Alpha manga/anime
characters.formDifferences: Ryu fully consumed by the Satsui no Hado: physically demonic (red glowing eyes, fangs, darkened skin) and far more powerful, gaining Akuma-style lethal techniques such as the Shun Goku Satsu (Raging Demon), the Metsu Hadoken and the Ashura Senku, at the cost of his humanity and self-control.
characters.summary: Evil Ryu is a hypothetical version of Ryu who has embraced the Satsui no Hado. He is much more powerful than base Ryu and uses Akuma's Raging Demon, but loses his compassion and finds his dark side very hard to control.

mechanisms: Ashura Senku: glides across the battlefield while temporarily invulnerable

weaknesses: The Power of Nothingness counters the Satsui no Hado: Gouken used it to seal Ryu's dark power in Street Fighter IV
The Shun Goku Satsu does not affect soulless foes such as Seth
limitations: Power comes at the expense of his humanity; he struggles to control his dark side mid-fight
Prolonged full use risks permanent possession by the Satsui no Hado

sources.supports: Evil Ryu as a version of Ryu who embraced the Satsui no Hado (Alpha 2, Capcom vs. SNK, SSFIV AE); physical changes; loss of humanity; prolonged use leads to permanent possession; Gouken sealed it with the Power of Nothingness in SFIV; Evil Ryu defeats Sagat, Birdie and Adon (Alpha manga), destroys Rosanov (Alpha: The Animation), and is defeated by Asura (Asura's Wrath).
Evil Ryu is much more powerful and can use the Raging Demon, at the cost of his humanity; Metsu Hadoken; Ashura Senku invulnerable glide; Shun Goku Satsu does not affect soulless foes like Seth.
Ryu gave in to the Satsui no Hadou during the Sagat fight and landed the Metsu Shoryuken that scarred Sagat.

feats.claim: Landed a near-fatal Metsu Shoryuken on Sagat after giving in to the Satsui no Hadou, leaving his chest scar.
feats.citation: Street Fighter (as retold in later games)

notableResults.note: Also defeated Birdie and Adon in the same manga.
Destroyed Rosanov.
Asura defeats Evil Ryu.

unknowns: The Satsui no Hado page says users in general gain telekinesis and flight; this is not shown for Evil Ryu specifically, so no tags are proposed.
Manga, anime and crossover results are separate continuities from the games.

characters.continuity: Street Fighter V (2016) and Arcade Edition: Ryu's Mu no Ken
characters.formDifferences: Ryu with the Power of Nothingness (Mu no Ken), the counterpart of the Satsui no Hado. In Street Fighter V he converts the dark Hado into it; his attacks become much more powerful and he can separate his soul from his body to avoid attacks like the Raging Demon, but the state has a time limit and needs concentration.
characters.summary: Power of Nothingness Ryu has reached the Mu no Ken state that Gouken first mastered. In Street Fighter V he converts the Satsui no Hado into it, and his Hadoken infused with the Power of Nothingness destroyed M. Bison's body at the end of A Shadow Falls.

mechanisms: Can separate his soul from his body to avoid attacks like the Raging Demon

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
limitations: The form has a time limit and cannot last for long periods
Holding it requires concentration that is hard to find mid-fight

sources.supports: The Satsui no Hado is the antithesis of the Power of Nothingness; in Street Fighter V Ryu completely converted the Dark Hado into the Power of Nothingness via Hado Kakusei.
A Shadow Falls finale: Ryu hits Bison with a Hadoken infused with the Power of Nothingness and Bison's body cracks and falls apart; his Denjin Hadoken shields Chun-Li and Li-Fen from debris.
Power of Nothingness form: much more powerful attacks, greater awareness, separating soul from body to avoid the Raging Demon; time limit and concentration requirement.

feats.claim: Destroyed M. Bison's body with a Power of Nothingness-infused Hadoken.
feats.citation: Street Fighter V: A Shadow Falls

feats.claim: Shielded Chun-Li and Li-Fen from reactor debris with his Denjin Hadoken.
feats.citation: Street Fighter V: A Shadow Falls

notableResults.citation: Street Fighter V: A Shadow Falls
notableResults.note: Final battle; Bison had already collapsed on one knee when Ryu's infused Hadoken destroyed his body.

unknowns: Gemini's electric-control tag was removed: the opened sources do not describe the Denjin Hadoken as electric.
How exactly Ryu attains the state in SFV (beyond Hado Kakusei conversion) is not detailed in the opened sources.

characters.continuity: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell series (Ubisoft), Splinter Cell through Blacklist
characters.summary: Sam Fisher is a former Navy SEAL and the first Splinter Cell field operative of the NSA's Third Echelon, later commander of Fourth Echelon. He is a stealth infiltrator trained in Krav Maga, knife fighting and ambidextrous shooting, using the SC-20K rifle, the Five-seveN pistol and gadgets such as sticky cameras, sonar goggles and a portable EMP generator.

techniques: SC-20K rifle with 40mm launcher (sticky shockers, gas grenades)

mechanisms: Stealth and concealment, especially in darkness

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
mobility: Swims and stays underwater for long periods

sources.supports: Navy SEAL and Third Echelon/Fourth Echelon background; stealth (silent movement, concealment, marking multiple targets); Krav Maga, knife fighting, ambidextrous shooting; SC-20K, Five-seveN, knives, portable EMP generator and sonar goggles (Conviction); named targets Kombayn Nikoladze, Admiral Otomo, Emile Dufraisne, Tom Reed, Andriy Kobin, Majid Sadiq.

feats.claim: Moves silently, conceals himself and marks multiple targets for takedown from concealment.
Captured Majid Sadiq at Site F.

notableResults.note: Killed during the JBA deep-cover operation.
Defeated and imprisoned, not killed.
Captured and interrogated.

campaignTags.claim: Documented stealth skills: silent movement, concealment, and marking targets from concealment in the dark.
First Splinter Cell field operative; served undercover inside the JBA terrorist group.
Uses sticky cameras, sticky shockers, sonar goggles and a portable EMP generator.

unknowns: The opened source does not mention the trademark tri-focal night-vision goggles, so they are not listed.
Several assassinations (Nikoladze, Masse, Soth) are not tied to a named game on the page and are not recorded as results.

characters.continuity: Metroid series (Nintendo), Metroid through Metroid Dread
characters.summary: Samus Aran is a bounty hunter raised by the Chozo, who integrated their DNA into hers. She wears the Chozo Power Suit, a bio-mechanical armor that can assimilate many weapons and functions, including an arm cannon, missiles, the Morph Ball and bombs. She has defeated Mother Brain, Ridley, Kraid, Metroid Prime and Raven Beak.
weaknesses: After the Metroid-based vaccine in Metroid Fusion she inherits the Metroids' weakness to cold

sources.supports: Power Suit as 'a bio-mechanical armor with the ability to assimilate many weapons and functions' given by the Chozo; Chozo DNA integration; missiles, Morph Ball and bombs; victories over Mother Brain, Ridley (incl. Meta Ridley and X-infected Ridley), Kraid, Metroid Prime, Dark Samus, SA-X and Raven Beak; inherited Metroid weakness to cold after the Fusion vaccine.

feats.claim: Absorbed the SA-X after it helped her defeat the Omega Metroid.

notableResults.note: In Super Metroid the Metroid Hatchling drained Mother Brain's energy before Samus destroyed her.

notableResults.citation: Metroid; Super Metroid; Metroid Prime; Metroid Prime 3; Metroid Fusion
notableResults.note: Repeated victories, including Meta Ridley and an X-infected Ridley.
Destroyed his X Parasite form.

campaignTags.claim: Wears the Chozo Power Suit, a bio-mechanical armor that assimilates weapons and functions.
Advanced Chozo powered armor; under the owner ruling, powered armor earns tech.

unknowns: Gemini's 'gadgets' tag was removed: the weapons are integrated suit functions, already covered by powered-armor and tech.
Space Jump, Screw Attack and Speed Booster are not described in the opened source.
The fabricated feat 'destroys entire planetary ecosystems single-handedly' was not restored.

characters.formDifferences: Samus in the Gravity Suit, found outside the Wrecked Ship after Phantoon is defeated. It lets her move freely underwater and cuts damage taken by 25% (75% combined with the Varia Suit).
characters.summary: Gravity Suit Samus is Samus Aran in Super Metroid's Gravity Suit, which removes the underwater movement penalty needed to explore Maridia and Ridley's Hideout and adds damage reduction on top of the Varia Suit.

mechanisms: Gravity Suit: 25% damage reduction, 75% combined with the Varia Suit

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources

sources.supports: Super Metroid: acquired outside the Wrecked Ship after Phantoon restores power; lets Samus 'move freely underwater', required for Maridia and Ridley's Hideout; reduces damage by 25%, 75% combined with the Varia Suit.
Super Metroid victories over Ridley, Kraid and Mother Brain (after the Metroid Hatchling drained her energy).

notableResults.note: Fought in Ridley's Hideout, which requires the Gravity Suit.
The Metroid Hatchling drained Mother Brain's energy before Samus destroyed her.

campaignTags.claim: Wears the Chozo Power Suit in its Gravity Suit configuration.
Advanced powered armor; under the owner ruling, powered armor earns tech.
The Gravity Suit lets her move freely underwater and is required to explore Maridia.

unknowns: Lava or magma protection is not confirmed for Super Metroid in the opened source, so it is not listed.

characters.formDifferences: During the final fight with Raven Beak, Samus's Metroid DNA fully awakens and her Gravity Suit turns into the Metroid Suit. It drains a large amount of energy from Raven Beak and his ship and gives her the Hyper Beam, a terrain-penetrating laser that is the only weapon able to kill X Parasites outright.
characters.summary: Metroid Suit Samus is Samus after her Metroid DNA awakens during the Raven Beak fight. Her raw Metroid-style suit drains energy and fires the Hyper Beam, with which she destroyed Raven Beak X. The suit was neutralized when she absorbed the X Parasite carrying Quiet Robe's DNA.

mechanisms: Drains energy from attackers and their machinery (absorbed energy from Raven Beak and his ship)

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
limitations: Its energy drain would have stopped her ship from leaving the planet intact
The Hyper Beam reportedly disables missiles, the Grapple Beam and the Omega Cannon

sources.supports: After fully awakening her Metroid DNA while fighting Raven Beak, Samus's Gravity Suit turns into the Metroid Suit; the Hyper Beam penetrates terrain, is the only weapon that kills X Parasites outright, and was used twice to destroy Raven Beak X; absorbing the X with Quiet Robe's DNA neutralized the suit.

Awakened 'full Metroid ability' drains a large amount of energy from Raven Beak and his spaceship; the energy-draining suit would stop her jet from leaving intact; Quiet Robe's sacrifice returns her suit to normal.

feats.claim: Drained a large amount of energy from Raven Beak and his spaceship.
Fired the Hyper Beam, a terrain-penetrating laser that kills X Parasites outright.

notableResults.note: Raven Beak had nearly suffocated her before the awakening; she destroyed his X-mutated form with two Hyper Beam shots.

conditional.dependsOn: Awakened Metroid DNA; neutralized when she absorbed the X Parasite carrying Quiet Robe's DNA

campaignTags.claim: The Metroid Suit is her Power Suit transformed by awakened Metroid DNA.
Advanced powered armor with an arm cannon; under the owner ruling, powered armor earns tech.

unknowns: Whether she stole Raven Beak's beam is fan speculation; the in-game Samus Screen says the Hyper Beam combines her own Arm Cannon abilities.

characters.formDifferences: Samus's suit after the Omega Pirate falls on her and Phazon seeps in, causing viral corruption. It gives complete protection from Blue Phazon, dramatically increases shielding, and enables Hyper-Mode and the Phazon Beam needed to defeat Metroid Prime.
characters.summary: Phazon Suit Samus is Samus in the corrupted suit she gains from the Omega Pirate battle in Metroid Prime. It shields her from Blue Phazon and enables the Phazon Beam, which she used to defeat Metroid Prime, who then tore the suit off her and later became Dark Samus.
weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
limitations: Protects fully only against Blue Phazon; more potent types of Phazon still damage her

sources.supports: Formed when the Omega Pirate fell on Samus and Phazon seeped into her suit; complete protection from Blue Phazon but more potent Phazon still damages; dramatically increased shielding; enables Hyper-Mode and the Phazon Beam required to defeat Metroid Prime; Metroid Prime pulls the suit off after its defeat and later becomes Dark Samus.

notableResults.note: The suit formed when the Omega Pirate fell on her during their battle.
The Phazon Beam was required to defeat it; after its defeat it pulled the Phazon Suit off her, leaving her in the Gravity Suit.

campaignTags.claim: Wears the Phazon-corrupted Chozo Power Suit.
Advanced powered armor; under the owner ruling, powered armor earns tech.

unknowns: Gemini's feat 'absorbs concentrated Phazon energy to overload enemy targets' is not described in the opened source and was not kept.
Exact conditions for activating the Phazon Beam are not described in the opened source.
